diagnosis: Progress is decaying to $\sim 5\times10^{-7}$ per program because every top worker seeds from `best.npy`/`record.npy` and makes small perturbations, so all are re-polishing the same basin. The image shows that basin is not actually jammed: at the $10^{-9}$ threshold there is only one exact contact pair and 66 rattlers, while the next $\sim$400 pairs form a plateau only $3$–$6\times10^{-8}$ below the max. A rigid isolated optimum in $S^{11}$ needs on the order of $68\cdot 11-\dim SO(12)=682$ independent active constraints, so the current code is a floppy, amorphous smooth-surrogate optimum, not a true rigid minimax configuration. The missing structural property is therefore a dense, balanced contact graph (and possibly exploitable symmetry/algebraic structure), not merely a slightly lower value of the same configuration.

diagnosis: Our best code is still essentially the published record's basin polished by LSE+LP, with total gain only $1.8\times10^{-5}$ in 65 programs and most gains shrinking to $10^{-9}$--$10^{-7}$. The image shows just one pair within $10^{-9}$ of the maximum and 66 nominal rattlers, yet roughly 400 pairs lie within $\sim2\times10^{-6}$, so it sits on a broad, unequally-loaded near-contact plateau rather than at a jammed optimum. A rigid minimax optimum should have hundreds of exactly tied contacts—on the order of the $68\cdot11-66=682$ effective tangent degrees of freedom—with a nonnegative equilibrium stress, typically enforced by symmetry or a few-distance algebraic structure. Without that rigidity/equalisation, every LP step is soon blocked by the near-contact shell while no step equalises it, and random delete-reinsert kicks slide back to the same fingerprint.
